html:
Burundi became independent from Belgium on 1 July 1962 as a constitutional monarchy under King Mwambutsa IV, separate from Rwanda, which became independent the same day as a republic.

The United Nations had hoped to keep Ruanda-Urundi as one state, but the two had gone different ways. In Burundi the monarchy still stood above Tutsi and Hutu, while in Rwanda the revolution had overthrown it.

The balance did not last. Prime ministers were killed, a Hutu coup attempt in 1965 was crushed, and in 1966 the army officer Michel Micombero abolished the monarchy and set up a republic run by Tutsi officers, which led to the Ikiza of 1972.
sum: Burundi became independent from Belgium on 1 July 1962 as a constitutional monarchy under King Mwambutsa IV, separate from Rwanda, which became independent the same day as a republic.
